results: GET /healthz is now a web-shell liveness response only ({"status":"ok","scope":"web-shell"}) and no longer signals engine or storage readiness; the supervisor, clone smoke and benchmark wait on /readyz instead.

GET /readyz probes web index.html, the loopback engine /healthz, the enabled storage surface and every enabled provider on each request and returned 200 ready for a real Go engine with the C05-backed sensor store; repeating launch after a full restart reached ready again.

Required failures are typed and visible: an unreachable or malformed engine produced engine_unavailable, a failing sensor surface storage_unavailable, and a failing certificate provider provider_certificates_unavailable with HTTP 503 status not_ready.
Optional provider failure (updates) produced HTTP 200 status degraded with providersReady:false while the engine and storage stayed ready; the optional failure is logged at warn level.

The diagnostics sample carried the sentinels from the Authorization header, the query string and the upstream credential body through the failing readiness path, and none appeared in the serialized /api/diagnostics response or any log message.

Logs are transition-based: a repeated probe of an unchanged state added no entries and no drops, while 40 alternating readiness transitions exercised the ring down to 32 entries, dropped at least 8, and the serialized entries stayed within the declared 8192-byte bound.
A missing dist/web/index.html made the web component itself not ready (HTTP 503, web_assets_unavailable) and added one typed log entry.

Invalid readiness configuration fails closed at construction: an unknown storage surface and a declared podman provider are rejected with explicit errors rather than placeholder readiness; the server source is restricted to loopback engine URLs and does not follow redirects.

The full repository checks passed: 6 targeted readiness tests, 94 Node tests through npm check, 195 engine anchors with 0 failing events, 6 Python tests, repository contracts, no diff whitespace errors and the real clean-clone smoke (including npm setup, Go race tests, event validation and unified startup).

rollback_or_recovery_observation: The change is additive to the local supervisor and serve-web routes plus documentation, fixtures and tests. Reverting the C29 files restores the previous /healthz body and removes /readyz and /api/diagnostics without touching accepted C05/C16/C17/C18 data, schemas, migrations, .env files or Dockerfiles. No persisted diagnostics state exists; a restart or revert simply recreates or removes the in-memory ring.
observed_limitations: Local Linux single-operator profile only; readiness covers the web shell, the loopback Go engine, the enabled storage surface and enabled certificate/update providers.
Rootless Podman and the isolated decoy are engine CLI surfaces, not web-supervised components; they are not probed, and declaring podman as a readiness provider is rejected.
Diagnostics are per web-server instance and reset on restart; they are not durable audit records or a substitute for C05/C17 evidence.
The C29 integration suite exercised the failure paths with local synthetic upstreams for provider status; the ready path used the real engine and authoritative store.
Browser rendering, hosted GitHub Actions, push, deployment and release were not exercised, and no C30 clean-host workflow or C40 artifact claim is made.

The recorded source identity precedes the progress, handoff and generated-project bookkeeping edits; no commit was created, so the final working-tree identity is not the recorded implementation identity.
The machine's go env sets GOSUMDB=off, so engine-spawning Node suites require GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.2 GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org; all results above used that documented environment.
